questions.question:
Select the most appropriate options to fill in the blanks.

_________ are used in load cells and proving rings to measure _______ produced.

options.text: Linear Variable Differential Transformer (LVDT); strain by the force
Strain gauges; force by the strain
Capacitive transducers; force by the strain
Piezoelectric transducers; strain by the force

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Strain gauges**(option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Strain gauges__ are used in load cells and proving rings.
 
• These devices measure strain produced by the force applied.
 
• When force is applied, strain gauges detect the deformation and convert it into electrical signals.
 
• They are highly sensitive and provide accurate readings of force and strain.
 
• Strain gauges are widely used in engineering applications to measure material deformation under stress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Linear Variable Differential Transformer (LVDT):**
 
 
• LVDTs are used for measuring linear displacement.
 
• They work on the principle of mutual inductance.
 
 
 
• **Capacitive transducers:**
 
 
• These transducers measure displacement, pressure, and other quantities by detecting changes in capacitance.
 
• They are not used for measuring strain in load cells or proving rings.
 
 
 
• **Piezoelectric transducers:**
 
 
• Piezoelectric transducers generate electrical charge in response to mechanical stress.
 
• They are commonly used in dynamic measurements such as vibration and acceleration.
 
 
</ul

• Light doping in the base allows minimal recombination.
 
• Moderate doping in the collector enables effective carrier collection.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: If a body falls freely under gravity from rest, what fraction of its initial potential energy has been converted into kinetic energy when it has fallen to half of its initial height?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1) 1/2.

Here's a step-by-step explanation:

 
• **Initial Potential Energy:** Let the initial height of the body be 'h'. The initial potential energy (PEi) is given by PEi = mgh, where 'm' is the mass of the body and 'g' is the acceleration due to gravity.
 
• **Height After Falling:** The body falls to half of its initial height, so the new height is h/2.
 
• **Potential Energy at New Height:** The potential energy (PEf) at the new height is: PEf = mg(h/2) = (1/2)mgh.
 
• **Change in Potential Energy:** The change in potential energy is: ΔPE = PEi - PEf = mgh - (1/2)mgh = (1/2)mgh.
 
• **Kinetic Energy:** According to the law of conservation of energy, the loss in potential energy is equal to the gain in kinetic energy (KE). Therefore, KE = ΔPE = (1/2)mgh.
 
• **Fraction of Initial Potential Energy:** The fraction of the initial potential energy converted into kinetic energy is: KE / PEi = ((1/2)mgh) / (mgh) = 1/2.

Therefore, half of the initial potential energy has been converted into kinetic energy.

questions.question: A 60-W lightbulb operates on a 120-V source. What is the current flowing through the bulb?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __0.5 A**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Power formula:__ Power (P) = Voltage (V) × Current (I).
 
• Given power is 60 W and voltage is 120 V.
 
• Using the formula, Current (I) = Power (P) / Voltage (V).
 
• Current (I) = 60 / 120 = 0.5 A.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is 0.5 A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• Ohm's Law states that Voltage (V) = Current (I) × Resistance (R).
 
• It provides a relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in an electrical circuit.
 
 
 
• **Power in Electrical Circuits:**
 
 
• Electrical power is measured in watts (W).

• L.V.D.T.__ stands for Linear Variable Differential Transformer.

questions.question: The brightness of LED depends upon _____; when source voltage is much _____ than diode voltage, then the brightness of the LED is approximately constant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __current**(greater)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The brightness of an LED__ depends on the current passing through it.
 
• When the source voltage is much greater than the diode voltage, the brightness of the LED becomes approximately constant.
 
• LEDs are current-driven devices, and their brightness increases with higher current flow until saturation.
 
• Excessive current can damage the LED or reduce its lifespan.
 
• Proper resistors are used in circuits to limit the current through the LED to a safe value.
 
• Temperature has a less significant effect on LED brightness compared to current.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **LED Characteristics:**
 
 
• LEDs have a forward voltage drop, typically ranging from 1.8V to 3.3V, depending on the material and color of the LED.
 
• Current through the LED is controlled using a resistor in series with the LED in most circuits.
 
 
 
• **Applications of LEDs:**
 
 
• LEDs are widely used in indicators, displays, and lighting applications due to their energy efficiency.
 
• They are available in various colors, including red, green, blue, and white, offering versatile usage options.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding Lenz's Law?

options.text: The induced current always opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it.
The induced current always assists the change in magnetic flux that produced it.
Lenz's Law does not relate to electromagnetic induction.
The direction of the induced current depends on the amount of magnetic flux.

questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Lenz's Law**

**Definition:** Lenz's Law, formulated by Heinrich Friedrich Emil Lenz in 1834, is a fundamental principle in electromagnetism. It states that the direction of the induced current in a closed circuit is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it. This law is consistent with the principle of conservation of energy and Newton's third law of motion.

**Mathematical Expression:** Lenz's Law can be mathematically expressed as part of Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction:

**ε = -dΦ/dt**

Where:

 
• ε is the electromotive force (EMF) induced in the circuit.
 
• Φ is the magnetic flux through the circuit.
 
• dΦ/dt is the rate of change of magnetic flux.
 
• The negative sign indicates the direction of the induced EMF opposes the change in magnetic flux.

**Working Principle:** According to Lenz's Law, when there is a change in the magnetic field within a closed circuit, an EMF is induced in such a direction that it creates a current whose magnetic field opposes the initial change in the magnetic field. This opposition is the key aspect of Lenz's Law, ensuring that the induced current always acts to counteract the change that caused it.

**Examples:**

 
• **Electromagnetic Braking:** In applications like magnetic braking systems, Lenz's Law is utilized to generate opposing magnetic fields that create resistive forces, slowing down the motion of a moving object.
 
• **Induction Heating:** In induction heating systems, Lenz's Law ensures that the induced currents generate heat by opposing the change in the magnetic field, effectively heating the material.
 
• **Electric Generators:** In electric generators, Lenz's Law governs the direction of the induced current, ensuring the generated EMF opposes the change in magnetic flux as the generator operates.

__
 
• Dead time__ refers to the delay period between a change in input quantity and the start of the instrument's response.
 
• It is an important performance parameter of measuring instruments.
 
• Shorter dead time indicates faster responsiveness and better efficiency of the instrument.
 
• Instruments with longer dead time are less suitable for dynamic measurements.
 
• Dead time can be reduced with advanced sensors and processing techniques.
 
• Understanding dead time is crucial for accurate calibration and system design.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Response Time:**
 
 
• It is the total time taken by an instrument to respond to a change in input.
 
• Response time includes both dead time and the time required to reach a steady-state.
 
 
 
• **Settling Time:**
 
 
• It is the time taken by an instrument to stabilize within a certain percentage of the final value after a change in input.
 
• Instruments with shorter settling times are ideal for dynamic applications.
 
 
 
• **Accuracy:**
 
 
• Accuracy refers to the closeness of the measurement to the true value.
 
• Precise calibration enhances measurement accuracy.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
In the given logic circuit, if the initial input is 0, then what will be the output of A and B, respectively?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9d9fb3ec2e6e58819c57120e04c06855efdf13d173c5bdf5111699bfff0e7e31.png]
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

 

**Step-by-Step Analysis:**

 
• **Initial Input:** The initial input to the logic circuit is 0.
 
• **AND Gate:** If the input 0 is fed into an AND gate with another input (let's assume it is also 0 for simplicity), the output of the AND gate will be 0 (since 0 AND 0 = 0).
 
• **OR Gate:** If the input 0 is fed into an OR gate with another input (let's assume it is also 0), the output of the OR gate will be 0 (since 0 OR 0 = 0).
 
• **NOT Gate:** If the input 0 is fed into a NOT gate, the output will be 1 (since NOT 0 = 1). However, if the NOT gate is not directly involved in determining A and B, we can ignore this for now.
 
• **Outputs A and B:** Based on the combination of AND and OR gates with the initial input 0, both outputs A and B will be 0.

Therefore, the correct option is 0, 0, which corresponds to Option 1

questions.question: The SI unit for measuring very large distances, such as astronomical distances, is ______________.
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**SI Unit for Measuring Astronomical Distances**

**Definition:** The SI unit for measuring very large distances, such as astronomical distances, is the light-year. A light-year is the distance that light travels in one year in a vacuum. It is commonly used in astronomy to express the vast distances between stars and other celestial objects.

**Working Principle:** Light travels at a constant speed of approximately 299,792 kilometers per second (km/s) in a vacuum. Over the course of a year, this speed translates to a distance of about 9.46 trillion kilometers (5.88 trillion miles). This enormous distance is what we refer to as one light-year.

**Advantages:**

__
 
• Provides a convenient way to express extremely large distances that are otherwise difficult to comprehend.
 
• Widely accepted and used in the field of astronomy, making it a standard unit for scientific communication.

**Disadvantages:**

 
• Not an SI base unit, which can sometimes lead to confusion in scientific contexts where SI units are preferred.
 
• The concept of a light-year may be difficult for the general public to grasp due to its sheer magnitude.

**Applications:** The light-year is primarily used in astronomy to describe distances between celestial objects, such as stars, galaxies, and quasars. It helps astronomers and astrophysicists convey the scale of the universe in a meaningful way.

**Correct Option Analysis:**

The correct option is:

**Option 4:** Light-year

This option is correct because the light-year is specifically defined as the distance light travels in one year, making it an appropriate unit for measuring astronomical distances. It is widely used in the field of astronomy to describe the vast expanses of space between stars and galaxies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Important Information__**

To further understand the analysis, let’s evaluate the other options:

**Option 1:** Metre

The metre is the base unit of length in the International System of Units (SI). While it is a fundamental unit for measuring distances, it is not practical for expressing astronomical distances due to the immense scales involved. A metre is too small a unit to effectively convey the vast distances between celestial bodies.

**Option 2:** Kilometre

The kilometre is a unit of length equal to 1,000 metres. Although it is more practical than the metre for measuring larger distances on Earth, it is still not suitable for astronomical distances. The distances between stars and galaxies are so vast that using kilometres would result in impractically large numbers.

**Option 3:** Astronomical Unit

The astronomical unit (AU) is a unit of length defined as the average distance between the Earth and the Sun, approximately 149.6 million kilometers. While the AU is useful for measuring distances within our solar system, such as the distances between planets, it is not commonly used for interstellar or intergalactic distances. For these larger scales, the light-year is more appropriate.

**Conclusion:**

Understanding the appropriate units for measuring astronomical distances is crucial for accurately describing the vastness of space. The light-year, as explained, is the distance light travels in one year and is widely used in astronomy for this purpose. While other units like the metre, kilometre, and astronomical unit have their uses, they are not suitable for expressing the immense distances between stars and galaxies. The light-year provides a practical and standardized way to convey these distances in scientific communication.

questions.question: A car of mass m accelerates uniformly from rest under a constant force F. After traveling a distance d, what is the kinetic energy of the car?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2) F×d.

Here's how to derive that:

 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:** The work done on an object is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.
 
• **Work Done:** Work is defined as force multiplied by the distance over which it acts: W = F × d.
 
• **Kinetic Energy:** The car starts from rest, so its initial kinetic energy is zero. Therefore, the final kinetic energy is equal to the work done on the car.

Therefore, the kinetic energy of the car after traveling a distance d is F × d.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the microprocessor 8085 is NOT correct?

options.text: It has serial I/O control, which allows serial communication.
It has a mechanism by which it is possible to increase its interrupt handling capacity.
It can be used to implement three chip microcomputers with supporting I/O devices like IC 8155 and IC 8355.
It does not provide control signal (IO/M, RW, WR) to control the bus cycles, hence external bus controller is required.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Microprocessor 8085__ is an 8-bit microprocessor developed by Intel.
 
• It provides serial I/O control, enabling serial communication.
 
• It has a mechanism to increase interrupt handling capacity through vectored interrupts.
 
• With supporting I/O devices like IC 8155 and IC 8355, it can be used to implement compact microcomputers.
 
• However, it provides control signals (IO/M, RW, WR) to manage bus cycles, eliminating the need for an external bus controller.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• It has five interrupt lines: TRAP, RST7.5, RST6.5, RST5.5, and INTR.
 
 
 
• **Serial Communication:**
 
 
• 8085 supports serial communication through SID (Serial Input Data) and SOD (Serial Output Data) lines.
 
• These lines allow exchange of data between the microprocessor and peripheral devices.
 
 
 
• **Supporting ICs:**
 
 
• IC 8155 offers additional I/O ports and a timer.
 
• IC 8355 provides programmable memory and I/O ports.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:

_____ error occurs as the value of flux density is different for the same value of current when increasing and decreasing.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Hysteresis**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hysteresis__ occurs in magnetic materials due to the lagging of magnetic flux density behind the magnetizing force.
 
• This phenomenon is observed when the value of flux density differs for the same value of current during increasing and decreasing cycles.
 
• The hysteresis loop, also known as the B-H curve, represents this relationship graphically.
 
• It leads to energy loss in the form of heat during magnetization and demagnetization cycles.
 
• Hysteresis is a critical factor in the design of transformers and other magnetic devices to minimize energy losses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Frequency:**
 
 
• Refers to the number of cycles per second in an alternating current or electromagnetic wave.
 
• Measured in Hertz (Hz).
 
 
 
• **Friction:**
 
 
• Friction is a resistive force that opposes the motion of two surfaces in contact.
 
• It is irrelevant to magnetic flux density behavior.
 
 
 
• **Temperature:**
 
 
• Changes in temperature can affect material properties but are not directly related to hysteresis.
 
• It influences factors like resistance and thermal expansion in electrical systems.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements for Piezoelectric transducer is correct?

options.text: Piezoelectric transducer can be used for the measurement of static displacement only.
Piezoelectric transducer can be used for the measurement of dynamic displacement only
Piezoelectric transducer can be used for the measurement of both static and dynamic displacement.
Piezoelectric transducer cannot be used for the measurement of both static and dynamic displacement.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Piezoelectric transducer can be used for the measurement of dynamic displacement only**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Piezoelectric transducer__ is used to measure dynamic parameters.
 
• It works based on the piezoelectric effect, which generates an electrical charge in response to mechanical stress.
 
• This transducer is not suitable for static displacement measurement due to charge leakage over time.
 
• Applications include measuring vibration, pressure, and acceleration in dynamic systems.
 
• Piezoelectric materials used include quartz, ceramics, and certain polymers.
 
• The transducer provides high sensitivity and accuracy for dynamic measurements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Advantages:**
 
 
• High-frequency response enables accurate measurement of dynamic parameters.
 
• Compact size and ease of installation.
 
• Wide range of applications in industrial and scientific fields.
 
 
 
• **Limitations:**
 
 
• Cannot measure static displacement due to charge leakage.
 
• Requires careful handling to avoid damage to the piezoelectric material.
 
 
</ul
